messages.content: I want to settle the air choices for Nashville and Raleigh now. Keep the Monday 6:00 p.m. dinner, Tuesday campus meetings, Wednesday transfer, Thursday forum opening, and Saturday breakfast ending around 10:30 fixed.
I’ll compare the full three-leg cost, travel time, arrival margin, and any effect on hotel nights. For Denver to Nashville, should I include all practical carriers?
Yes. Please include United when it’s competitive, along with the other sensible carriers; I don’t need it ranked first.

The two useful outbound choices are: Sunday, January 24, Southwest nonstop, 6:20-9:45 p.m., 2h25 elapsed, $214; or Monday, January 25, United via Houston, 7:05 a.m.-12:58 p.m., 4h53 elapsed, $176. The Sunday flight gives an overnight buffer but requires Nashville lodging January 24-27, three nights. The Monday flight avoids that extra night and reaches Nashville 5h02 before dinner, though the usable margin is closer to three and a half hours after deplaning and getting to the hotel.
The Monday connection seems reasonable. How does it affect the total compared with taking the Sunday nonstop?

Using the stronger Wednesday and Saturday choices, the Monday itinerary totals $504 in airfare. Substituting the Sunday nonstop raises airfare to $542 and adds a third Nashville hotel night. The Sunday option is more resilient to disruption, but it costs $38 more before the added room charge.
Then use Monday unless one of the later legs makes that too risky. Compare Wednesday next.

Wednesday offers a Southwest nonstop from Nashville at 11:15 a.m., arriving Raleigh at 1:45 p.m.; 1h30 elapsed and $139. The cheaper American connection leaves at 3:40 p.m., changes in Charlotte, and arrives at 8:55 p.m.; 4h15 elapsed and $96. Both produce the same Raleigh stay, January 27-30, but the connection saves only $43 and removes nearly all of Wednesday’s preparation time before Thursday’s opening.
Take the midday nonstop. I need that afternoon more than I need the $43. Now compare the Saturday returns against the 10:30 breakfast finish.

The early return is American via Charlotte, 1:20-5:58 p.m., 3h38 elapsed, $151. It leaves only 2h50 from breakfast finish to departure, and roughly 50 minutes after allowing time to return downtown, collect luggage, drive to RDU, and meet a conservative airport arrival target. The evening United nonstop is 6:10-8:12 p.m., 4h02 elapsed, $189. It costs $38 more but leaves 7h40 after breakfast and about 5h40 after those same ground-time allowances. Neither option requires Saturday-night lodging.
The 1:20 connection is too tight. Choose the evening nonstop. What is the exact combined plan and how does it compare with the cheapest possible combination?

Selected air plan: Monday, January 25, Denver-Houston-Nashville, 7:05 a.m.-12:58 p.m., $176; Wednesday, January 27, Nashville-Raleigh nonstop, 11:15 a.m.-1:45 p.m., $139; Saturday, January 30, Raleigh-Denver nonstop, 6:10-8:12 p.m., $189. Airfare totals $504. The cheapest combination of the six listed choices is $423: Monday connection, Wednesday late connection, and Saturday early connection. Your selection costs $81 more, preserves Wednesday afternoon, and provides a workable Saturday airport margin.
Good. Record those flights, but don’t ticket them until the live schedules, operating carriers, fare rules, baggage terms, and seats are checked. Confirm the hotel dates they establish.

Recorded, not ticketed. Nashville is now two nights: check in Monday, January 25, and check out Wednesday, January 27. Raleigh is three nights: check in Wednesday, January 27, and check out Saturday, January 30. The selected flights preserve the Monday dinner, Tuesday meetings, Wednesday preparation time, Thursday opening, and Saturday breakfast. The Residence Inn will need luggage storage after checkout because the return is in the evening. Before purchase, I’ll verify flight numbers, live times, operating carriers, fare restrictions, carry-on and checked-bag terms, seat availability, and the final $504 air total.
